title: Nation-building
examples: What were the biggest challenges Singapore faced after independence?
How did Singapore manage to build its economy from scratch?
Can you explain the role of housing in building a nation?

explain.say: Today we look at how Singapore built itself into a modern nation.
First we look at housing, which helped people live together safely.
Next we study defence, which kept the nation secure from outside threats.
Then we examine the economy, which brought jobs and money to everyone.
In real life, building a modern city needs all three things working together.
A common mistake is thinking only money builds a nation successfully.

items: A nation needs more than just wealth.
People need safe places to live.
They also need to feel secure.

draw.text: Mistake: Money alone is not enough

faq.q: How important was housing in Singapore's development?
faq.a: Housing was very important because providing affordable homes allowed families to settle down and build stable communities.
asks: Did the government build all the homes?

faq.q: What does 'defence' mean in this context?
faq.a: Defence means protecting the country from threats, which includes having a strong military and safety plans.
asks: How did they keep Singapore safe?

faq.q: How did Singapore change its economy?
faq.a: Singapore changed its economy by not relying on just one thing, like trade or one industry.
asks: Did they become a trading center?
What industries did they focus on?

faq.q: Were these three areas developed at the same time?
faq.a: While they were all important, the focus often shifted depending on the immediate challenge the nation faced.
asks: Did one area come before the others?

faq.q: What was the biggest challenge they overcame?
faq.a: The biggest challenge was starting from having very few natural resources and being surrounded by other countries.
asks: What problem did they solve first?

facts: Public housing schemes provided affordable and modern homes for citizens.
A strong defence force was necessary due to Singapore's small size.
The economy grew by attracting international businesses and diversifying industries.
These efforts were key to transforming Singapore into a modern city-state.

quiz.say: What was a major part of building stable communities?

options.show: Public housing schemes provided stable shelter.
options.say: Public housing schemes provided stable shelter.

quiz.why: This shows the government actively provided the basic need for shelter.

wrong.0: This is an economic activity, not a physical structure.
wrong.1: Trade is economic, but housing addresses the physical living situation.
wrong.3: This relates to defence, not the immediate need for housing.

quiz.say: If a nation needs to protect itself, which area is most vital?

options.show: Maintaining a strong military and safety plan.
options.say: Maintaining a strong military and safety plan.

quiz.why: Defence is specifically about protecting the physical safety and sovereignty of the state.

wrong.0: Skyscrapers are part of the economy, not the core defence strategy.
wrong.1: This is an economic goal, not a defence measure.
wrong.2: This is an infrastructure improvement, but defence is about threat mitigation.

quiz.say: Which action best shows economic diversification?

options.show: Developing both electronics and finance sectors.
options.say: Developing both electronics and finance sectors.

quiz.why: Diversification means not depending on just one source of income or industry.

wrong.1: This shows reliance on one sector, which is risky.
wrong.2: This addresses housing, not the source of national income.
wrong.3: This is a defence measure, not an economic one.
